correctness.rationale: Strict two-point median dominance yields a finite lazy stochastic influence matrix; an oriented boundary proof shows exactly max(1,J) closed communicating classes, with standard finite-chain convergence and a fixed-space dimension equal to their count. Counting cyclic nonempty R/L runs yields the full exact mass function of J and the special consensus formula; binomial limits yield the sparse transition. The separate equal-weight boundary has a sharp four-median obstruction by direct cohesive-set reasoning. The embedded checker exhausts 10,844 ring-type instances, testing independently enumerated cohesive subsets, graph-reachability closed classes, and both full law and closed consensus law under two exact rational parameter triples. Finite tests support, not replace, the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The ring is a motivated tractable benchmark for disagreement in heterogeneous social dynamics. An exact model-specific statistic gives the dimension of persistent disagreement and its complete probability distribution, rather than just a yes/no eventual-consensus criterion, with an exact interpretable sparse scaling and delicate half-weight boundary. This is independently useful for quantifying network reliability, not merely an arbitrary finite enumeration; no empirical calibration or new general consensus theorem is asserted.
